concepts.title: Prime Numbers and Divisor Counting
concepts.definition: A prime is a whole number above 1 whose positive divisors are just itself and 1; any larger whole number with an extra divisor is composite, and 1 falls in neither group.
concepts.key_idea: If n = p**a * q**b, each exponent offers one more choice per prime, so multiply one-plus-exponent over all primes.
question_patterns: find the number of positive divisors of 360 from its prime factorization
how many divisors does 2^4 * 3^2 * 7 have in all
test whether 971 is prime by checking divisors up to its square root
count the total divisors of 1080
is 437 a prime or a composite number, give a reason
write 104568 as a product of primes

solution_steps.action: add one to the exponent of the first prime
solution_steps.explain: each prime contributes exponent plus one choices

solution_steps.action: add one to the exponent of the second prime
solution_steps.explain: repeat for every distinct prime

solution_steps.action: add one to the exponent of the third prime
solution_steps.explain: a missing prime has exponent zero and contributes factor one

solution_steps.action: multiply the three factors
solution_steps.explain: divisor count is the product of the one-plus-exponent terms

concepts.title: GCD from Prime Factorizations
concepts.definition: The greatest common divisor of two numbers is the largest integer dividing both; comparing factorizations, it keeps each shared prime raised to the smaller of its two exponents.
concepts.key_idea: Minimum exponents of the common primes multiplied together give the gcd.
question_patterns: find the gcd of 4680 and 15708 using their prime factorizations
compute the highest common factor of 105 and 120
two numbers factor as 2^3 * 3^2 * 5 and 2^2 * 3 * 7 * 11; what is their gcd
find gcd(210, 495) by comparing exponents of common primes
what is the greatest common divisor of 4680 and 15708
check whether 3 and 17 are coprime

solution_steps.action: take the smaller exponent of the first prime
solution_steps.explain: the gcd carries whichever power of p occurs less often

solution_steps.action: take the smaller exponent of the second prime
solution_steps.explain: same comparison for the next shared prime

solution_steps.action: multiply the prime powers
solution_steps.explain: the product of these minimum powers is the gcd

concepts.title: Euclid Division Algorithm for GCD
concepts.definition: The Euclid division algorithm finds the highest common factor of two positive integers by repeated division: divide, keep the remainder, then divide the previous divisor by that remainder. Because every remainder is smaller than the divisor, the remainders shrink strictly and the ladder must terminate; the last nonzero remainder is the gcd.
concepts.key_idea: The last nonzero remainder left on the ladder is the gcd.
concepts.textbook_ref: am11_001_numbers_quantification.txt, section 1.3 Euclid GCD algorithm ladder for 15708 and 4680
question_patterns: use Euclid algorithm to find the gcd of 4680 and 15708

apply the remainder ladder to get gcd(4052, 12576)
find the greatest common divisor of 15708 and 4680 without factoring them
run the division algorithm on 324 and 48 and state the hcf

solution_steps.action: divide b by a and keep the remainder
solution_steps.explain: first rung of the ladder

solution_steps.action: divide a by r1
solution_steps.explain: shift the pair down one rung

solution_steps.action: divide r1 by r2
solution_steps.explain: repeat the modulo step

solution_steps.action: divide r2 by r3
solution_steps.explain: remainders keep shrinking

solution_steps.action: divide r3 by r4
solution_steps.explain: continue while remainders are nonzero

solution_steps.action: divide r4 by r5
solution_steps.explain: the next remainder would be zero, so this value is the last nonzero remainder

solution_steps.action: declare the last nonzero remainder as the gcd
solution_steps.explain: stop once a remainder of zero would follow

concepts.title: Euler Totient and RSA Key Parameters
concepts.definition: For an RSA modulus n built from two distinct primes p and q, the totient counts the integers below n that are coprime to n as (p-1)(q-1); a public exponent e is chosen coprime to this count and the private exponent d undoes it.
concepts.key_idea: Multiply the two reduced primes to count the usable key values.
concepts.textbook_ref: am11_001_numbers_quantification.txt, section 1.3 RSA example with p = 71, q = 101
question_patterns: an RSA setup picks p = 71 and q = 101; find the modulus n and the totient

how many integers from 1 to 34 are coprime to 35

find the public modulus when the secret primes are 3 and 11

solution_steps.action: multiply the two secret primes
solution_steps.explain: the modulus n = pq is made public

solution_steps.action: reduce each prime by one and multiply
solution_steps.explain: phi(n) = (p-1)(q-1) counts numbers coprime to n

concepts.title: Modular Arithmetic and Remainder of Powers
concepts.definition: Two integers are congruent modulo m when division by m leaves them the same remainder; a power can be reduced after every multiplication without disturbing the final remainder.
concepts.key_idea: Reduce after each squaring or multiplication so the numbers stay small.
concepts.textbook_ref: am11_001_numbers_quantification.txt, section 1.3 congruences, Euler theorem a^phi = 1 mod m
question_patterns: find the remainder when 3^5 is divided by 7
what is the remainder of 2^10 modulo 5

solution_steps.action: square the base
solution_steps.explain: write the exponent as a sum of doublings plus a leftover

solution_steps.action: reduce the square modulo m
solution_steps.explain: smaller stand-in with the same remainder

solution_steps.action: multiply the reduced square by itself
solution_steps.explain: this covers the exponent 4

solution_steps.action: reduce and multiply the leftover base factor
solution_steps.explain: exponent 5 = 4 + 1

concepts.title: Binary to Decimal Conversion
concepts.definition: A base 2 numeral stores coefficients of powers of two; scanning the bits left to right and doubling the running total before adding each bit rebuilds the base 10 value.
concepts.key_idea: Each step doubles what has been read and drops in the next bit.
concepts.textbook_ref: am11_001_numbers_quantification.txt, section 1.4 binary expansion of 23456 and (1010101010) = 682
question_patterns: convert the binary number 101101110100000 to decimal notation

solution_steps.action: take the leading bit and fold in the second
solution_steps.explain: running total starts at the first bit

solution_steps.action: double the total and add the next bit
solution_steps.explain: Horner step for the third bit

solution_steps.action: double the total and add the next bit
solution_steps.explain: repeat for every remaining bit

solution_steps.action: double the total and add the last bit
solution_steps.explain: the final total is the base 10 value

concepts.title: Decimal to Binary by Repeated Halving
concepts.definition: Divide the number by 2 again and again, writing down each remainder; the remainders read from last to first spell out the base 2 numeral.
concepts.key_idea: The remainder column read bottom to top is the binary numeral.
question_patterns: write 23456 in binary form
convert 100 to base 2 by repeated division

write the base 2 numeral equal to 682

solution_steps.action: divide by 2 and record the remainder
solution_steps.explain: the remainder is the units bit

solution_steps.action: divide the quotient by 2 again
solution_steps.explain: each remainder is the next place value bit

solution_steps.action: stop when the quotient reaches zero
solution_steps.explain: no powers of two remain

solution_steps.action: read the remainders from bottom to top
solution_steps.explain: the highest bit is found last

concepts.title: Multiplying Complex Numbers
concepts.definition: For z1 = a1 + b1 i and z2 = a2 + b2 i, expand like binomials and replace i squared with -1; the pieces regroup into a new real part and a new imaginary part.
concepts.key_idea: Cross terms build the new imaginary part; the b1 b2 term flips sign.
question_patterns: find the product (1 + i)(2 + 3i) in a + bi form
multiply 3 + 2i by 1 - 4i
compute z1 z2 for z1 = 1 - i and z2 = 3 + i
evaluate the square of 1 + i

solution_steps.action: multiply the real parts and subtract the imaginary product
solution_steps.explain: i squared turns b1 b2 into -b1 b2

solution_steps.action: add the two cross products
solution_steps.explain: these carry the factor i

solution_steps.action: square the new parts and add
solution_steps.explain: prepares the modulus of the product

solution_steps.action: take the square root
solution_steps.explain: the modulus of a product is the product of moduli

concepts.title: Conjugate and Modulus of a Complex Number
concepts.definition: Changing the sign of the imaginary part gives the conjugate of z; the modulus is the distance of z from the origin, computed from the two parts.
concepts.key_idea: z times its conjugate equals the squared modulus, a real nonnegative number.
concepts.textbook_ref: am11_001_numbers_quantification.txt, section 1.5 zz-bar = a^2 + b^2 and |1 + i| = sqrt(2)
question_patterns: find the modulus of 1 - i

solution_steps.action: square both parts and add
solution_steps.explain: z z-bar collapses to a real sum of squares

solution_steps.action: take the nonnegative square root
solution_steps.explain: this is the modulus

concepts.title: Powers of Iota on the Four Cycle
concepts.definition: Since i squared equals -1, powers of iota repeat in a block of four; the remainder of the exponent on division by 4 selects the value among 1, i, -1 and -i.
concepts.key_idea: Cycle values 0, 2 give the real answers 1 and -1; odd cycles keep one factor of i.
question_patterns: find the value of i raised to 100
simplify i^402
evaluate i^96
what does i^4n equal for a whole number n

solution_steps.action: divide the exponent by 4 and keep the remainder
solution_steps.explain: the cycle position repeats every four powers

solution_steps.action: convert an even cycle position to a numeric value
solution_steps.explain: cycle 0 gives 1 and cycle 2 gives -1

concepts.title: Laws of Indices
concepts.definition: Powers obey short rules: same-base products add exponents, same-base quotients subtract them, a power of a power multiplies them, and a zero power gives 1 while a negative power inverts the base.
concepts.key_idea: Combine exponents by the index laws before evaluating any number.
concepts.textbook_ref: am11_001_numbers_quantification.txt, section 1.6 indices rules and examples 2^3.2^2 = 2^5
question_patterns: simplify 2^3 * 2^5 and give its value

solution_steps.action: add the exponents of the same-base product
solution_steps.explain: index law for multiplication

solution_steps.action: divide by the remaining power
solution_steps.explain: index law for division subtracts exponents

concepts.title: Logarithm Product Rule with Given Values
concepts.definition: A logarithm states the power that produces a given number from a base; the log of a product splits into a sum of logs, and a repeated factor drags its multiplier out front.
concepts.key_idea: Break the target number into known factors, then add multiples of their given logs.
concepts.textbook_ref: am11_001_numbers_quantification.txt, section 1.7 properties of logarithms, log 2 = 0.3010 style tables

solution_steps.action: write the target as a product of powers of the known factors
solution_steps.explain: 12 = 2 squared times 3

solution_steps.action: add the log of the remaining factor
solution_steps.explain: product rule turns multiplication into addition

concepts.title: Antilogarithm via Powers of Ten
concepts.definition: The antilog reverses a logarithm: if x is the log of y to base 10, then y is 10 raised to x; splitting x into whole and fractional pieces rebuilds y as a whole power times a fractional power.
concepts.key_idea: Whole part fixes the size, fractional part fixes the significant digits.
concepts.textbook_ref: am11_001_numbers_quantification.txt, section 1.7 anti-logarithm paragraph after log properties
question_patterns: find the antilog of 2.4771

solution_steps.action: raise 10 to the fractional part
solution_steps.explain: the fractional part gives the leading digits

solution_steps.action: raise 10 to the whole part
solution_steps.explain: the whole part is the power of ten scale

solution_steps.action: multiply the two pieces
solution_steps.explain: antilog = whole power times fractional power

concepts.title: Richter Scale Amplitude Comparison
concepts.definition: Earthquake magnitude sits on a base 10 logarithm of the wave amplitude over a fixed reference wave, so every whole step on the scale multiplies the amplitude by ten.
concepts.key_idea: Subtract the two magnitudes first; ten to that difference is the amplitude factor.
concepts.textbook_ref: am11_001_numbers_quantification.txt, section 1.8 Richter scale R = log(A/A0), Chile 1960 magnitude 9.5
question_patterns: how many times larger is the amplitude of a magnitude 8.5 earthquake than a magnitude 6.3 one

solution_steps.action: subtract the smaller magnitude from the larger
solution_steps.explain: the difference drives the factor

solution_steps.action: raise ten to the difference
solution_steps.explain: each unit of Richter difference is a tenfold amplitude step

concepts.title: Exponential Growth Models
concepts.definition: When a quantity multiplies by a fixed factor every fixed interval, its size equals the starting amount times that factor raised to the number of elapsed intervals.
concepts.key_idea: Divide the elapsed time by one interval to count the doublings, then scale the start value.
concepts.textbook_ref: am11_001_numbers_quantification.txt, section 1.8 bacteria b = 200(2)^(t/20) and population P = 4.7(1.02)^t
question_patterns: a bacteria colony doubles every 20 hours starting from 200 cells; how many cells after 60 hours

solution_steps.action: divide the elapsed time by one doubling interval
solution_steps.explain: counts how many times the factor applies

solution_steps.action: raise the growth factor to that count
solution_steps.explain: two for doubling, three for tripling

solution_steps.action: multiply the starting amount
solution_steps.explain: scales the colony size
